description: Three tasks over the self-authored `textkit` sample repository: a separator-collapse bug fix, an unimplemented word-wrap feature, and a truncation fix with a regression trap. Hidden acceptance tests are injected at grading time only.

tasks.title: slugify emits repeated and dangling separators
tasks.description: slugify maps every non-alphanumeric character to the separator individually, so runs of punctuation or whitespace produce repeated separators and the result can start or end with one.
tasks.problem_statement:
`textkit.slugify` produces malformed slugs.

Reproduction:

    >>> from textkit import slugify
    >>> slugify("Hello,  World!")
    'hello---world-'

Expected: 'hello-world'

The function should treat a *run* of non-alphanumeric characters as a single separator, and the returned slug must not begin or end with a separator. A string with no alphanumeric characters at all should produce an empty slug. This must work for any single-character separator passed via the `sep` argument, not just the default '-'.

Do not change the existing public signature or the ValueError raised for a multi-character separator.
acceptance_criteria: Runs of non-alphanumeric characters collapse to a single separator
The slug never starts or ends with the separator
Input with no alphanumeric characters yields an empty string
Behaviour holds for a custom single-character separator
Existing tests in tests/test_slug.py continue to pass
hints: Track whether the previous emitted character was already a separator.

tasks.title: Implement greedy word wrapping in wrap_text
tasks.description: wrap_text is declared with a documented contract but raises NotImplementedError.
tasks.problem_statement:
`textkit.wrap_text(text, width)` is declared in `src/textkit/wrap.py` but raises NotImplementedError. Implement it according to its docstring.

Required behaviour:

- Return a list of lines, each at most `width` characters long.
- Split the input on runs of whitespace; a run of whitespace is a single word separator, so `wrap_text("a   b", 10) == ["a b"]`.
- Pack words greedily: fill the current line while the next word still fits, then start a new line.
- A word longer than `width` cannot fit on any line, so hard-split it across consecutive lines.
- Input that contains no words returns an empty list.
- Raise ValueError when `width` is less than 1.
- Lines must carry no leading or trailing whitespace, and word order must be preserved.

Example: `wrap_text("the quick brown fox", 10)` returns `["the quick", "brown fox"]`.
acceptance_criteria: Words are packed greedily and kept in order
Words longer than width are hard-split
Whitespace runs collapse to a single separator
Empty or whitespace-only input returns an empty list
hints: str.split() with no argument already collapses whitespace runs.

tasks.title: truncate returns strings longer than the requested limit
tasks.description: truncate appends its suffix after cutting to the full limit, so the result exceeds the limit. Fixing it naively breaks the existing short-string behaviour, which is the regression this task guards.
tasks.problem_statement:
`textkit.truncate(text, limit, suffix='...')` promises a result of at most `limit` characters, but it appends the suffix *after* cutting to `limit`:

    >>> from textkit import truncate
    >>> truncate("abcdefghijklmnop", 10)
    'abcdefghij...'   # 13 characters, limit was 10

Required behaviour:

- The returned string is never longer than `limit`.
- Text that already fits is returned unchanged, with no suffix.
- When the text must be cut, the suffix is included inside the budget, and the cut is made at a word boundary if one exists within that budget. `truncate("hello wonderful world", 12)` must return `'hello...'`.
- There is no trailing whitespace before the suffix.
- When `limit` is less than or equal to the suffix length, return the suffix truncated to `limit` (so `limit=0` yields an empty string).
- A negative `limit` still raises ValueError.

The existing tests in `tests/test_truncate.py` describe behaviour that must not change.
acceptance_criteria: Text that fits is returned unchanged
Cut happens at a word boundary when one exists in the budget
limit <= len(suffix) returns the suffix truncated to limit
Existing tests in tests/test_truncate.py continue to pass
hints: Reserve len(suffix) characters from the limit before cutting.
str.rfind(' ') locates the last word boundary in the budget.
